sources.title: Peru Ministry of Culture: Ashaninka
sources.note: Direct institutional entry read. Geography, Instituciones sociales and Conocimientos y prácticas tradicionales. Public passages describe documented practices, not universal 1492 customs.

sources.title: Peru Ministry of Culture: Asheninka
sources.note: Direct entry: modern recognition of distinct history, language and identity. Used for identity boundary, not to transfer Asheninka practices to Ashaninka.

sources.title: José Pimenta / Instituto Socioambiental: Ashaninka
sources.note: Direct full ethnographic entry. História no Peru: Comércio e guerra; Colonização e revoltas indígenas; O Peru independente. Do not adopt broad ancient ethnic attribution or conflate present Asheninka classification with older umbrella usage.

sources.title: Peru Truth and Reconciliation Commission: Indigenous peoples and the Ashaninka
sources.note: Primary 2003 report, chapter 2.8, public Equipo Nizkor mirror. Printed page 241/PDF page 1 explicitly calls casualty/displacement figures estimates; printed 259 to 260/PDF pages 19 to 20 discusses food and refuge.

sources.title: Enrique Rojas Zolezzi: Ashaninka spinning and weaving (1999)
sources.note: Direct original article, Anthropologica 17, pp.117 to 134. Printed pp.118 to 119/PDF pages 2 to 3 spinning; pp.120 to 121/PDF pages 4 to 5 loom and household construction.

sources.title: Museum of International Folk Art: Cushma, A.1995.93.1255
sources.note: Direct catalogue identifies Ashaninka, Peru, circa 1970, cotton/paint, 122 by 104 cm; no named maker or precise community.

sources.title: Kemito Ene: The hope of cacao
sources.note: Direct producer account; discussion of direct marketing, intermediary prices and technical advice. A community enterprise account, not an independent profitability evaluation.

sources.title: Central Asháninka del Río Ene: Strategy to 2030
sources.note: Direct one-page 2024 strategy. Education baseline states only 50% of primary graduates reach secondary school; targets are not achievements. Governance and women/youth priorities support continuing community institutions.

sources.title: CARE: SAVIA maternal and child health programme (7 July 2025)
sources.note: Direct primary project report: more than 300 families, 14 named Ene communities, in-person and digital support, links to Satipo health network. Outcomes not established.

sources.title: TVPerú / IRTP: Pasonki Quipatsi documentary announcement (2022)
sources.note: Direct fetch failed, full indexed original resolved with query site.tvperu.gob.pe "Pasonki Quipatsi" "2022". Dated 12 October 2022, title and opening paragraph explicitly identify Ashaninka and translate Gracias Madre Tierra. This is a written contemporary programme title.

sources.title: ONIC: Wayuú
sources.note: Direct Indigenous national organisation entry, 3 May 2016. Geography, ranchería households and history. Avoid its obsolete population totals and overly categorical funerary description.

sources.title: Forero, Rúa Bustamante and Zambrano Ortiz: Beyond Animal Husbandry (2023)
sources.note: Direct open-access original, Human Ecology 51,627 to 640. Political Devolution supplies qualified historical synthesis; Methodology reports participant observation, microscopy and nine Colombian communities.

sources.title: UNESCO: Wayuu normative system applied by the Pütchipü’üi
sources.note: Direct nomination summary, inscribed 2010. Peaceful mediation and compensation, matrilineal clans and maternal uncles. Does not establish a single Wayuu national government.

sources.title: National Museum of Colombia: Wayuu hammock, September 2007
sources.note: Direct collection essay; twentieth-century cotton hammock E83-VI-496, 375 by 210 cm, La Guajira. Portable use, newborn hammock. Omit universal two-year puberty seclusion claim.

sources.title: Smithsonian NMAI: Wayuu hammock collected in 1931
sources.note: Direct museum catalogue. Gregory Mason 1931 collection, La Guajira, hemp/cordage, knotted; collection year is not manufacture date.

sources.title: Artesanías de Colombia: Wayuu weaving
sources.note: Direct craft institution account. Hamaca/chinchorro structures, separately woven fittings and named bags; contemporary craft description, not precontact crochet claim.

sources.title: UNICEF Colombia: Sin el agua no podríamos vivir (2024)
sources.note: Direct primary project report, 30 August 2024. Guarerapo tres, Estefany Ríos operates treatment of saline groundwater; Ayana’ajirawa since 2021, hygiene and latrines.

sources.title: UNICEF: Bicycles for Wayuu education and water access (2024)
sources.note: Direct 22 April 2024 announcement about 18 April programme. 500 bicycles planned in Guarerapo/Jasaichon; avoid presenting all promised deliveries as verified completed.

sources.title: David and Linda Captain: Wayuu-English-Spanish dictionary (2019)
sources.note: Direct SIL/Webonary original PDF, title/copyright 2019. Entry akuꞌulawaa, dictionary p.17 of 161, PDF page28/index27: Akuꞌulaashi taya sünain ashajaa. / I’m beginning to write. / Empiezo a escribir. Introduction explicitly identifies Latin-script materials.

batchIdentityNotes.scope: Public opening distinguishes separately indexed Asheninka. Historical sources sometimes use Campa/Ashaninka broadly, so the draft avoids transplanting Gran Pajonal-specific material or assigning millennia-old remains a secure modern ethnicity.
